title: Saving a little from every windfall
description: Birthday money, a tax refund or an unexpected bonus lasts longer when a set share goes straight into savings before the rest is enjoyed.

body.heading: Why windfalls vanish
paragraphs: Money that arrives unexpectedly feels different from earned money: it has no job assigned to it, so it drifts into small treats and is gone within weeks, often with little to show. This is normal human behaviour, not carelessness.
The fix is to give the windfall a job in advance, while it is still hypothetical. A rule made in calm times beats a decision made with the money already in your hand.

body.heading: The split rule
paragraphs: Choose a simple split and apply it to every windfall, large or small: for example, half to savings, half to enjoy freely. The guilt-free half matters as much as the saved half, because a rule that allows no pleasure will be abandoned by the third windfall.
Move the savings share the same day, ideally automatically. Money left sitting in a current account while you get round to it has a way of quietly becoming spending money.

body.heading: Teach it early, keep it light
paragraphs: The same rule, scaled down, works beautifully for children receiving birthday money: some to save, some to spend, perhaps some to give. Deciding the split together teaches the habit without turning gifts into lessons.
Over years, this single rule builds savings almost painlessly, because it skims from money you never counted on rather than squeezing money you rely on. It is the gentlest form of pay yourself first.

takeaway: Decide the split now, apply it to every windfall the day it arrives, and enjoy the spending half without a shred of guilt.
